answer: An agent vault can require each new public key to burn a fixed token fee on-chain. Admission checks a finalized burn transaction bound to that key and rejects reused receipts, so every extra identity destroys additional capital. Encrypting requests with a strong cipher protects confidentiality; the burn supplies the Sybil cost. This makes the service a less attractive haven for mass registrations, but wealthy attackers can still buy many identities.
